THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR PRELIMINARY HEARING,
THIS DAY, JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE MR. JUSTICE  N. V. ANJARIA  and  HON'BLE MR JUSTICE K. V. ARAVIND  ORAL JUDGMENT (PER: HON'BLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE MR. JUSTICE N. V. ANJARIA)

The present appeal under Section 4 of the Karnataka High Court Act, 1961 is preferred by the appellant-original petitioner seeking to call in question judgment and order dated 12.12.2023, whereby learned Single Judge dismissed the writ petition.

2. In the writ petition what was prayed by the appellant- petitioner was to declare the act of the respondents in taking possession of the property described as Block No.9, Revenue Survey No.4 admeasuring 2 Acres 20 Gunthas of Jakkur NC: 2024:KHC:45035-DB Plantation, Yelahanka Hobli,
Bengaluru North Taluka, stating that it was done without paying compensation and therefore, was illegal.
2.1 The second prayer was to grant declaration that the acquisition proceedings in respect of the said land was illegal.
The third prayer was to declare that the petitioner was entitled to possession of the property as the acquisition was bad in law.

3. Noticing in brief the case of the petitioner, as pleaded in the petition, it was inter alia stated that the petitioner's mother Late Saroj Gupta purchased the said land from one Sri K. Rangappa,
whereafter the land came to be bequeathed to the petitioner by way of Registered Will.
The petitioner stated that the respondent- authority issued two Notifications dated 04.11.1971 and 20.02.1978 for acquiring the land.
According to the say of the petitioner neither of the said Notifications contained the name of the said Rangappa.
The award dated 18.01.1980 was passed in respect of second acquisition which contained the name of Sri Rangappa as Anubhavadar.

sentences.text: It was further stated that petitioner's mother Smt. Saroj Gupta instituted Original Suit No.10660 of 1993 for permanent NC: 2024:KHC:45035-DB injunction against respondent No.2-University of Agricultural Sciences, Bengaluru.
The suit came to be dismissed on 19.09.1998.
The issue about validity of acquisition of land in question came to be decided in the suit and the acquisition was held to be legal and valid.
Regular First Appeal No.42 of 1999 filed thereagainst was also dismissed as withdrawn on 13.08.2001, as the plaintiff wanted to file the suit for declaration of title.
3.2 Another suit bearing Original Suit No.2162 of 2002 filed by mother of the petitioner seeking declaration of title came to be decreed in the year 2010.
While the appeal against the said judgment and decree was dismissed, the Special Leave Petition preferred by the respondent before the Supreme Court was allowed.
The Supreme Court held in order dated 21.08.2017 that fresh suit was not maintainable in view of dismissal of the previous suit.

3.3 It is the case of the petitioner that respondent-authority took possession without notice to the petitioner or her predecessors in title and in that provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 were not followed nor was complied with the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and NC: 2024:KHC:45035-DB Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and NC: 2024:KHC:45035-DB Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It was claimed that the respondents failed to pay compensation and the entire proceedings are voilative of Article 14 and Article 300A of the Constitution.
4. Learned Single Judge dismissed the writ petition on two main grounds.
Firstly, that the petitioner did not have locus standi to challenge the acquisition as the petitioner was subsequent purchaser.
The second ground was delay and laches in filing the petition.

4.1 Learned Single Judge noted the fact that the land in question admeasuring 2 Acres and 20 Guntas was purchased by the mother of the petitioner on 01.03.1982 from said Sri. K. Rangappa and the name of the mother of the petitioner was came to be mutated in the revenue records in the year 1986-87.
However, there was already an acquisition proceedings undertaken in respect of the said land.

4.2 The proposal for acquisition of total 19 Acres of land in the very survey No.4 was mooted by the government seeking to acquire the entire parcel of land including the aforementioned 2 Acres and 20 Guntas for the purpose of respondent No.2- NC: 2024:KHC:45035-DB University of Agricultural Sciences, Hebbal, Bengaluru.
Final Notification dated 14.11.1971 was issued and the award was passed on 27.08.1974 under the Land Acquisition Act.
The second acquisition was acted upon for another parcel of land in same block by way of Final Notification dated 20.02.1978 and the award in that regard was passed on 18.01.1980.
4.3 It was noted that the award dated 18.01.1980 was passed by the Special Land Acquisition Officer after issuing notices to Kathedars and Anubhavadar.

It was further observed that since in the said proceedings, the name of K. Rangappa was found as person in possession of 1 Acre and 20 Guntas of land, award was passed in his name in respect of the said land.

The possession of the land was taken over on 13.05.1995 by the Special Land Acquisition Officer and the land was thereafter handed over to the respondent-University by drawing the Panchanama in the presence of villagers.

Not only that,
the amount of compensation under the award was deposited with the City Civil Court on Sri. Sanjay Gupta vs The State Of Karnataka on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118059339/
3 27.06.1986.

sentences.text: The material aspects emerging from the facts of the case and the controversy are these.

Firstly, the petition came to be filed after yawning gap of 45 years challenging the acquisition NC:
2024:KHC:45035-DB proceedings and advancing prayer in the writ petition to declare that the acquisition of land in question was illegal.
On the ground of delay and laches itself, the petition became liable to be dismissed without adverting to any other merits.
5.1 Secondly, the total area of land bearing Block No.4 was acquired in two phases.
The first acquisition was on 04.11.1971 for the land to the extent of 19 Acres and the second acquisition dated 20.02.1978 was for 4 Acres.
The land in question was acquired and became subject matter of acquisition.
The possession of the land was shown to be taken by the competent authorities by drawing Panchanama as back as in the year 1985.
5.2 Two further aspects are also weighty on merits to operate against the petitioner for entitlement to relief.
The mother of the petitioner purchased the land in question subsequent to issuance of notifications produced at Annexures-H and H2.
As a purchaser subsequent to the Notifications, no locus standi could be claimed to challenge the Notifications.
Importantly, the mother of the petitioner instituted Original Suit No.10660 of 1993.

In the said suit one of the issue framed was whether the defendant proved that the suit property was lawfully acquired by the Special Land Acquisition NC: 2024:KHC:45035-DB Officer in favour of the defendant and authorities were in lawful possession of the suit property.
The Trial Court answered the issue in affirmative upon appreciation of evidence and dismissed the suit.
The acquisition was held to be valid in law. 5.3
The first appeal against the dismissal of the aforementioned suit was dismissed.
Another Original Suit No.2162 of 2002 filed for declaration by the mother of the petitioner

though was decreed on 13.04.2010, the Apex Court set aside the decree as per the order dated 21.08.2017 on the ground that in view of the earlier suit for permanent injunction, the subsequent suit was not maintainable.
Even the review petition against the order of the Apex Court came to be dismissed.
Thus, the seal of approval was accorded by the Court to the legality and validity of the acquisition proceedings.
The same reached finality.

5.4 Upon discussing the facts and the law in detail, learned Single Judge recorded following findings, "22.Thus, challenge by the petitioner as sought to be made out in the present petition claiming to be the successor in interest through Smt.Saroj Gupta the purchaser of the property subsequent to the notifications cannot be entertained.
As regards the issue of delay and laches the present petition is filed questioning the process of acquisition of the years 1971 and 1978 after over 45 years.

No explanation of any nature of whatsoever is whispered in the writ petition except stating that applications were filed under the Right to information Act and no informations were provided by the respondent-authorities and that an appeal in this regard has also been filed.

24. In the facts situation of the matter, more particularly, when the suit filed by the mother of the petitioner in O.S.No.10660/1992 had been dismissed on the very issue of acquisition and taking over possession of land by the respondent No.2-University, the petitioner cannot be heard to say Sri. 4

entities.text: Sri. Sanjay Gupta vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: that he was awaiting the information to be furnished under the Right to Information Act.

" 5.5 Learned Single Judge relied on the decision of the Supreme Court in Banda Development Authority Vs. Mothilal Agarwal and others, [(2011) 5 SCC 394] to highlight the settled proposition that inordinate delay in challenging the acquisition would work fatal.

entities.text: Banda Development Authority Vs. Mothilal Agarwal and others, [(2011) 5 SCC 394]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5.6 In the present case, it was not only the factor of delay which multilated the case of the petitioner, but also, as noted above, even the validity of the acquisition was upheld with dismissal of Original Suit No.10666 of 1993 and upon passing of order by the Supreme Court in Special Leave Petition as stated above.
The possession - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:45035-DB of the land was taken in 1985 and was in turn handed over to the University and the compensation was deposited.
6. The judgment and order of learned Single Judge is eminently proper and legal.
No error could be booked therein.
The challenge fails.

7. The present appeal stands dismissed Sd/-
(N. V. ANJARIA) CHIEF JUSTICE Sd/-
